Before the fix, actual same-origin window.open copied the original tab identity, reproducing a shared writable journal owner. After Web Lock claiming, the same real opener flow assigned distinct live owner IDs. Each tab received a different complete engineering paragraph; both reloaded and independently recovered only their own marker. Saving A at revision 7 did not delete B recovery: B reloaded with its own marker, then its old-base save produced a durable conflict. Explicit comparison and draft rebase saved B at revision 8, preserving A as immutable revision 7. Both tabs ended saved; copied tab closed, original tab reloaded the latest saved material. No content review confirmation was made. Unsupported/rejected Web Locks use per-document fresh owners with prior-owner read-only recovery, validated by behavior tests.
cases.fallback_behavior_tests: Per-reviewer/material sessionStorage last-written-owner reference updates only after a successful local journal write. Two consecutive fallback reloads without edits still choose the prior own draft ahead of a different tab’s newer shared draft, with independent references for two materials and reviewer separation. The fallback retains its inherited legacy owner until actual records exist. Large journal ownership is not advertised before durable write succeeds. These fallback checks are behavioral tests; the real Chrome browser checks use Web Locks.
